controls.rationale: Memory pages holding keys, tokens and decrypted business data are written to swap and survive on disk after power-off.
controls.check: Every active swap area (/proc/swaps) and every swap /etc/fstab activates at boot is dm-crypt (crypttab), zram or a file on an encrypted filesystem; no swap is also compliant.

remediation.summary: Encrypt swap or replace it with zram.
remediation.manual: Random-key swap: add `swap /dev/<dev> /dev/urandom swap,cipher=aes-xts-plain64,size=512` to /etc/crypttab and point fstab to /dev/mapper/swap; or install zram-generator/zram-tools and disable disk swap (`swapoff -a`, remove it from fstab).

controls.title: LUKS volumes use LUKS2 with a memory-hard KDF
controls.rationale: LUKS1 and PBKDF2 key slots are far cheaper to brute-force on GPUs than argon2id; the volume is only as strong as its weakest key slot.
controls.check: `cryptsetup luksDump` of each crypto_LUKS device: version 2 and every key slot uses argon2id or argon2i.

remediation.summary: Convert and re-key the volume.
remediation.manual: Back up the header (`cryptsetup luksHeaderBackup`), then `cryptsetup convert --type luks2 <dev>` (offline) and `cryptsetup luksConvertKey --pbkdf argon2id <dev>` for each key slot.

controls.title: Crash dumps do not write process memory to disk
controls.rationale: systemd-coredump stores the full memory of crashed processes, secrets included, under /var/lib/systemd/coredump.
controls.check: Effective coredump configuration (`systemd-analyze cat-config systemd/coredump.conf`): Storage=none and ProcessSizeMax=0, or systemd-coredump not in use.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure core dump storage is disabled / Ensure core dump backtraces are disabled

remediation.summary: Set Storage=none and ProcessSizeMax=0 in a coredump drop-in.

controls.title: TLS and service private keys are not readable by others
controls.rationale: A readable TLS or service private key lets any local user impersonate the service or decrypt captured traffic.
controls.check: /etc/ssl/private and /etc/pki/tls/private (and their files) grant no permission to 'other'; *.key and *.pem private keys under /etc are not world-readable.

remediation.summary: Remove all 'other' permissions from the private key directories and files listed.

controls.title: Application data directories are not accessible to other users
controls.rationale: Database files, message queues and container storage hold business data in clear text on disk; any local account must not read them.
controls.check: Each existing directory of sdw_app_data_dirs grants no permission to 'other'.

remediation.summary: Remove all 'other' permissions from the listed data directories.

controls.title: User credentials at rest are private
controls.rationale: SSH keys, database passwords (.pgpass, .my.cnf), cloud credentials (.aws, .kube) and .netrc in a readable file are credentials handed to every local user.
controls.check: In each interactive home: .ssh is <= 0700; private keys, authorized_keys, .pgpass, .my.cnf, .netrc, .aws/credentials, .kube/config, .docker/config.json grant nothing to group/other.

remediation.summary: Remove group/other permissions from the listed credential files.

controls.title: The system-wide crypto policy is not LEGACY
controls.rationale: The LEGACY policy re-enables SHA-1 signatures, 1024-bit DH/RSA and TLS 1.0/1.1 for every library that follows the policy.
controls.check: `update-crypto-policies --show` is DEFAULT, FUTURE, FIPS or a sub-policy of them (RHEL-family and Fedora; skipped elsewhere).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure system wide crypto policy is not set to legacy

remediation.summary: Set the crypto policy to DEFAULT.
remediation.risk: Peers that only speak TLS 1.0/1.1 or SHA-1 lose connectivity.

controls.title: The system TLS library refuses protocols older than TLS 1.2
controls.rationale: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 rely on SHA-1/MD5 constructions and are deprecated by RFC 8996.
controls.check: Probed with the library itself: `openssl ciphers -s -tls1` / `-tls1_1` against the effective OpenSSL configuration (security level and MinProtocol).

remediation.summary: Raise the OpenSSL protocol floor.
remediation.manual: Set `MinProtocol = TLSv1.2` and `CipherString = DEFAULT:@SECLEVEL=2` in the [system_default_sect] of openssl.cnf (Debian/Ubuntu), or `update-crypto-policies --set DEFAULT` (RHEL-family).

controls.title: SSH offers no weak ciphers
controls.rationale: CBC-mode, 3DES, RC4 and Blowfish ciphers are exposed to plaintext-recovery and downgrade attacks (Terrapin, SWEET32).
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T ciphers contains no CBC, 3DES, arcfour, blowfish or cast128 cipher.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd Ciphers are configured

remediation.summary: Restrict Ciphers to AEAD/CTR ciphers supported by this sshd (chacha20-poly1305, aes-gcm, aes-ctr).
remediation.risk: Clients that only speak the removed algorithms (old SSH libraries, some network appliances) can no longer connect.

controls.title: SSH offers no weak message authentication codes
controls.rationale: MD5, SHA-1 and 64-bit MACs do not provide adequate integrity; encrypt-then-MAC variants are preferred.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T macs contains no MD5, SHA-1, RIPEMD or 64-bit UMAC.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd MACs are configured

remediation.summary: Restrict MACs to SHA-2 encrypt-then-MAC variants supported by this sshd.
remediation.risk: Clients that only speak the removed algorithms (old SSH libraries, some network appliances) can no longer connect.

controls.title: SSH key exchange uses no SHA-1 or small groups
controls.rationale: diffie-hellman-group1-sha1, group14-sha1 and group-exchange-sha1 rely on SHA-1 and, for group1, a 1024-bit group within reach of nation-state precomputation.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T kexalgorithms contains no SHA-1 based algorithm.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd KexAlgorithms is configured

remediation.summary: Restrict KexAlgorithms to hybrid post-quantum, curve25519 and SHA-2 groups supported by this sshd.
remediation.risk: Clients that only speak the removed algorithms (old SSH libraries, some network appliances) can no longer connect.

controls.title: SSH host keys and signatures are strong
controls.rationale: DSA keys and RSA keys under 3072 bits are below current recommendations; ssh-rsa signatures use SHA-1.
controls.check: Effective host keys (sshd -T hostkey, measured with ssh-keygen -l): no DSA, RSA >= sdw_ssh_min_rsa_bits; no ssh-rsa/ssh-dss in the accepted public key or host key algorithms.

remediation.summary: Replace weak host keys and drop SHA-1 signatures.
remediation.manual: Remove DSA host keys and HostKey lines pointing to them; regenerate RSA with `ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key` (clients will see a changed key: publish the new fingerprint), prefer ed25519. Remove ssh-rsa/ssh-dss from HostKeyAlgorithms and PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms.

controls.title: SSH prefers hybrid post-quantum key exchange
controls.rationale: Traffic recorded today can be decrypted once a cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists (harvest now, decrypt later). OpenSSH 9.0+ offers hybrid sntrup761/ML-KEM key exchange; ANSSI recommends hybrid post-quantum mechanisms.
controls.check: Effective: the first entry of sshd -T kexalgorithms is mlkem768x25519-sha256 or sntrup761x25519-sha512.

remediation.summary: Put the hybrid post-quantum algorithms first in KexAlgorithms (when this sshd supports them).

controls.title: SSH requires a second authentication factor
controls.rationale: A stolen key or password should not be enough to log in. OTP (TOTP/HOTP via pam_oath or pam_google_authenticator), FIDO2 hardware keys (sk-ed25519 with verify-required, pam_u2f) or key+password all qualify.
controls.check: Effective sshd -T: every AuthenticationMethods list combines two distinct factors (publickey, password, keyboard-interactive backed by an OTP/FIDO/push PAM module), or only FIDO2 sk-* public keys with verify-required are accepted.

remediation.summary: Enrol a second factor, then require it.
remediation.manual: TOTP: `apt install libpam-google-authenticator` (or `dnf install google-authenticator`), each user runs `google-authenticator`; add `auth required pam_google_authenticator.so` to /etc/pam.d/sshd; set `KbdInteractiveAuthentication yes` and `AuthenticationMethods publickey,keyboard-interactive`. FIDO2: users create `ssh-keygen -t ed25519-sk -O verify-required`; set `PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com,sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com` and `PubkeyAuthOptions verify-required`. Keep a second session open while testing. Not automated: enrolment is per user.

controls.title: Privilege escalation requires a second factor
controls.rationale: If an administrator's password is phished, sudo with a hardware key (pam_u2f) or OTP still blocks the attacker from becoming root.
controls.check: Effective PAM auth stack of sudo contains pam_u2f, pam_yubico, pam_oath, pam_google_authenticator or a push/RADIUS second-factor module.

remediation.summary: Add a second factor to /etc/pam.d/sudo.
remediation.manual: FIDO/U2F: `apt install libpam-u2f` (or pam-u2f), users run `pamu2fcfg > ~/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys`, add `auth required pam_u2f.so cue` before the common-auth include in /etc/pam.d/sudo. OTP: add `auth required pam_google_authenticator.so` instead. Test in a second root shell before closing the first.

controls.title: OTP seeds and FIDO key maps are protected
controls.rationale: An OTP seed file readable by others lets anyone generate valid codes: the second factor is gone.
controls.check: pam_oath usersfile (default /etc/users.oath) is root-owned and 0600; each user's ~/.google_authenticator and ~/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys is owned by the user and grants nothing to group/other. Skipped when no such file exists.

remediation.summary: Remove group/other permissions from the OTP/U2F secret files and fix their owners.

controls.title: The kernel runs in FIPS mode
controls.rationale: FIPS mode restricts the kernel and FIPS-aware libraries to validated algorithms; required for US federal and some regulated workloads.
controls.check: Runtime: /proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled = 1. Persistent: fips=1 on the next boot's kernel command line.

remediation.summary: Enable FIPS mode.
remediation.manual: RHEL-family: `fips-mode-setup --enable` and reboot. Ubuntu: requires Ubuntu Pro (`pro enable fips-updates`).
